newsitem.title: USA: San Francisco expands BankAmerica bond suit. [corrected 20:33 gmt]
newsitem.headline: San Francisco expands BankAmerica bond suit. [corrected 20:33 gmt]

text.p: San Francisco has amended its lawsuit against BankAmerica Corp. to include allegations that an employee at the nation's third-largest bank embezzled funds from its corporate trust accounts, attorneys for the city said Monday. (Corrects to make clear that one employee was involved.)

Both the city of San Francisco and the state of California have sued BankAmerica and its unit, Bank of America for allegedly overcharging bond issuers, failing to return unclaimed funds from bond accounts to the state and improperly investing funds from some of the accounts.
The state lawsuit claims hundreds of millions of dollars in damages.

The embezzlement claim involves a bank employee who allegedly took $693,000, Deputy City Attorney Don Tickle said. The charges were included in an amended complaint filed in San Francisco Superior Court on Friday.
A Bank of America spokesman said the embezzlement case was uncovered by the San Francisco-based bank years ago.

The bank maintains that it unintentionally overcharged the city and other issuers for trust services and retained some funds. The bank said it discovered the overcharges on its own and voluntarily refunded more than $5 million to its customers.
San Francisco city attorneys also alleged in the amended complaint that the bank's trust unit had been "chronically out of balance" since the 1970s.
In 1993, outside auditor Ernst & Young found that the bank underestimated its cash shortage at its corporate trust unit by $1.2 billion, Tickle said.
BankAmerica's stock rose $2 to $117.875 on the New York Stock Exchange at mid-afternoon.
